THE ONE DESIGN POINT worth carrying forward: the read-only guarantee is DSN-shaped, not open-flags-shaped. Against modernc.org/sqlite the 'file:' prefix is load-bearing (without it the driver consumes the query string itself and silently drops mode=ro, leaving a read-write connection), plain mode=ro on a CHECKPOINTED store creates a 32 KiB -shm and a zero-length -wal and leaves them behind, and immutable=1 is a silent STALE read when the store has WAL-resident rows ('no such table: cards'). So the exporter picks the DSN from the store's shape (WAL in use -> mode=ro; quiescent -> mode=ro&immutable=1) and proves it twice: a write must be refused on the connection, and the store's file hashes and file list must be identical before/after. title: [foreman:P3] .gitignore's `canopyd` pattern also matches the cmd/canopyd/ DIRECTORY, so any NEW file under it is silently unaddable
detail: `.gitignore:16` is the bare pattern `canopyd` (intended: the built binary at the repo root). Git matches that pattern against the DIRECTORY `cmd/canopyd/` too, so a new file added there is ignored: `git check-ignore -v cmd/canopyd/<new>.go` -> `.gitignore:16:canopyd` and `git add cmd/canopyd/<new>.go` exits 1 with 'The following paths are ignored by one of your .gitignore files: cmd/canopyd'. title: [foreman:P2] Token-tamper security test is non-deterministic: it tampered with a fixed "AA" suffix (no-op ~0.09% of runs) and with a TRAILING base64url character (2 spare bits, decoded bytes can be identical), so it demanded rejection for an unchanged valid token and reddened CI on a board-only commit
reasoning: Tick 494: CI run 35311008908 (commit 02cb8a0, board-only) went red in the short suite on TestReferenceSelectionSigner_RejectsTamperingAndForeignCallers/tampered_signature with Verify() error = <nil>. The product was correct - the verifier accepted an UNCHANGED, valid token. Reproduced deterministically and measured at HEAD: `token[:len(token)-2] + "AA"` is a no-op whenever the signature already ends in "AA" (19 no-ops / 20000 signings, ~0.095%), and mutating the trailing character does not reliably change the signature BYTES because 43 base64url characters carry 4 significant bits plus 2 spare bits and Go decodes them leniently. Filed as a P2 because a security test that fails ~1 run in 1000 teaches the fleet to ignore red, and because the same tamper shape can hide behind a green suite. Fix landed in the same pass (1574a3d).
worker_summary: foreman-direct, 1 commit 1574a3d (internal/service/multi_reference_test.go, +41/-1). tamperedToken() now flips the FIRST character of the signature segment (fully significant 6 bits) instead of overwriting the last two with the fixed "AA" suffix. Evidence: the targeted test FAILS in a -count=3000 loop with the old form and passes 3000/3000 with the new one; tamper no-op rate measured 0/20000 for the new helper vs 19/20000 for the old; package internal/service ok; build/vet/gofmt/golangci-lint clean; CI run 35311475715 GREEN on the fix and the rerun of the original red run 35311008908 also GREEN with no tree change, which is the flake signature.
foreman_note: The product was NOT at fault: the verifier correctly accepted an unchanged valid token that the test believed it had tampered with. The verifier is deliberately untouched - Go base64 spare-bit leniency is not a forgery path, since the MAC still authenticates the payload - so this is a test fix only. Reusable law: a tamper test must mutate material that is (a) guaranteed to differ at the STRING level and (b) significant at the BYTES level; a fixed-suffix overwrite fails (a) and a trailing base64url character fails (b). Do NOT re-dispatch.

title: [foreman:P3] Retrieved tier: the query is the node's whole content under plainto_tsquery AND semantics, so realistic messages retrieve nothing
detail: Phase 4a derives the retrieval query from the current node's full content (whitespace-collapsed, 300-rune cap) and the topic search runs it through PostgreSQL plainto_tsquery, which ANDs every non-stopword term. Live probe evidence (isolated canopyd, throwaway DB): the 3-term content 'zebra runbook cutover' matched the seeded topic 'Zebra Runbook Cutover' and folded in, while the earlier sentence-shaped content 'zebra migration runbook planning for the zebra cutover' matched NOTHING (the topic lacks 'planning') - so the tier works, but on natural prose it will usually return an empty set and spend nothing.
reasoning: The tier is honest either way (no fabricated hits, no wasted budget), but a retrieval feature that silently yields nothing on ordinary messages has low product value. Decide in phase 4b/4c: keep AND but derive a term-selected query (top-N content terms), or move to an OR/ts_rank query and let the compiler's relevance ordering cut the tail. Either way the decision belongs in the SPEC-IMPL-GAP-001 amendment, and the acceptance should be measured on real message shapes, not on crafted 3-word fixtures. RESOLVED tick 515, commit 17ae9a6: chose the OR/ts_rank route named in this row's own reasoning, but as an explicit FALLBACK behind the unchanged ALL-TERMS pass (precision is never traded for recall), with the query built from sanitized lexemes rather than raw content. The design decision is recorded in specs/SPEC-IMPL-GAP-001-context-compiler.md (phase 4c amendment, this tick). Row accepted: the tier now fires on sentence-shaped messages, which is what the row asked for (measurable on real message shapes, not 3-word fixtures).

title: [foreman:P2] The card SSE stream dies at the transport's 30s WriteTimeout, so the SPEC-PL-03 §9.3 heartbeat never reaches a client
detail: Proven against a HEAD-built scratch canopyd (scripts/scratch-instance.sh --port 8125, DB canopy_scratch_516_59ce8ee1, binary built from fadd3c4; instance dropped after): (1) a `curl -sN` stream on GET /api/v1/cards/{id}/events?after_sequence=1 received only the card_snapshot frame and then died — curl exit 18 ('transfer closed with outstanding read data'), server log 'in 30.001566726s'; (2) a python urllib capture on the same route (cursor 0) got snapshot + the replayed card_event and then ended at the SAME 30.0s boundary; the 45s-window variant captured no heartbeat either. The handler prepares a heartbeat body and the failure point is the write: internal/server/server.go:148 sets WriteTimeout: 30 * time.Second while internal/handler/card_events_handler.go:40 fixes cardSSEHeartbeatInterval = 30 * time.Second — the frame is written AT the deadline, writeSSEFrame returns an error and the handler returns without logging (handler loop, `case <-heartbeat.C:` branch). The repo already solved this exact class for the gateway feed: internal/handler/gateway_handler.go:359-361 uses a 20s ticker with the comment 'Heartbeat keeps the stream alive past the server's 30s WriteTimeout'. Client impact, measured on the shipped client half (tick 516): connection 'live' can never latch (it is set only by a heartbeat frame) and after 30s the stream closes cleanly, which frontend/src/lib/sse.ts surfaces as onClose — NOT an error — so the bounded retry never fires and the panel silently stops updating.

title: [foreman:P2] The global chi Timeout(60s) context cap ends every SSE stream (tree + card) cleanly at ~60s even after the DF-31 write-deadline fix
detail: Found while verifying DF-HERMES-CANOPY-31 (tick 517): internal/server/server.go:259 mounts r.Use(middleware.Timeout(60 * time.Second)) globally; chi's timeout middleware wraps every request context in context.WithTimeout(60s). Both streaming event loops (internal/handler/card_events_handler.go and internal/sse/sse_handler.go) return on ctx.Done, so a card or tree SSE stream now survives the 30s WriteTimeout (heartbeats DO reach the client and the 'live' state latches) but is still cut off cleanly at ~60s. The shipped client surfaces that clean close as onClose (NOT an error), so the bounded retry never fires and the panel silently stops updating — the same user-visible defect DF-31 fixed, one minute later. The judge-approved DF-31 regression test (TestCardSSE_SurvivesServerWriteTimeout) reads for 4x a 300ms WriteTimeout and never reaches 60s, so it cannot see this boundary. Fix is a small design decision, not a hot patch: exempt long-lived SSE routes from the global Timeout middleware (mount them before/outside it, or per-route skip) and keep the 60s cap for ordinary requests, OR record an owner decision that 60s is an intended session bound and then (a) document it in docs/API.md and (b) make the frontend treat a clean SSE close as a reconnectable event.
reasoning: Filing instead of hot-patching because moving routes out of a global middleware changes the request lifecycle for every surface and deserves an explicit decision; the DF-31 row fixed the transport deadline, this row owns the next bound in the same liveness chain.

title: [P1] The QA lane grades and closes a run CLEAN one minute into a 7-15 minute battery: single collect attempt, filed:0, real cells never pulled, agent left to TTL
detail:
dogfood run 2026-09-17 (target row trouble-qa) — QA lane field test

ROUTED from the trouble board row QA-LANE-6 (filed 2026-09-17 from a dogfood run against trouble-qa). Owner: this repo — bunker-qa.sh cites its own QA-HERMES-CANOPY-8 for the launch/collect split, so these harness defects belong here, not on the target repo's board. Original review notes:
Observed end to end on the targeted tick: `launch` cell written 22:10:15Z (battery started detached, toolchain-bootstrap OK / fresh-install in progress on the agent at 22:10:45Z), then `parse_cells` ran its ONE PHASE-B collect attempt at ~22:11Z, got RUNNING (early-exit, no destroy), and the pipeline went straight to `interpret` (22:11:13) and `file_findings` (22:11:19) -> verdict CLEAN, findings [], filed 0, summary 'phase-B collect has not reported results, so no findings are derivable'. The battery was ~1 minute into a 7-15 minute run; its later cells (ci-pass, chaos-*) were never collected, no ledger row records them, and the agent is left to its 4h TTL. This is the premature-completion pattern the QA lane exists to catch, implemented in the lane itself: the verdict is honest about having no evidence, but the RUN still terminates as CLEAN, so a failing CI/chaos cell produces no row, no gap, no retry. Design quotes (hermes-dagger examples/coding-hermes/qa.ts ~L150-190): 'PHASE A: LAUNCH, never wait ... Phase B (collect) runs at the top of parse_cells and pulls the cells once it has finished; if nothing collects it, the agent's TTL (default 4h) reclaims it.' Fix direction: poll collect to completion (bounded, e.g. until ~20 min) before interpreting, or emit an explicit UNVERIFIED/deferred row + a scheduled second pass so the finished cells reach the board; never let a still-running battery end as CLEAN.

title: [P0] MLS cross-member decryption is impossible: Encrypt derives the AES key from the SENDER's public key, Decrypt from the RECIPIENT's - any ciphertext is readable only by its sender, so workspace group messaging cannot deliver a message; the surface is RFC-9420-shaped but not MLS
detail: Reproduced live (dogfood 2026-09-20, HEAD 85eaf18, scratch DB :5438/:8098): Alice creates group (real Ed25519 pair), Bob joins via POST .../mls/groups/join (204, epoch 0->1), Alice encrypts 'secret for bob' (200, epoch 1), Bob decrypts -> 500 with server log 'mls: gcm open: cipher: message authentication failed'. Alice decrypting her OWN ciphertext round-trips fine. Root cause internal/mls/service.go: Encrypt aesKey = sha256(group_id || member(sender).EncryptionPublicKey); Decrypt aesKey = sha256(group_id || member(recipient).EncryptionPublicKey) - different keys by construction, and both derived from PUBLIC non-secret material (the code's own comment admits it: 'In a full MLS implementation, this would use the group's epoch secret'). No forward secrecy, no group key agreement, ratchet_tree ships null in GET .../mls/state, JoinGroup stores keys derived from client-supplied key_package bytes. Yet types/wire shapes advertise RFC 9420 ('mls_ciphertext_v1', cipher-suite string, 'opaque RFC 9420 application-message representation'), and AGENTS.md claims 'MLS group encryption for workspace collaboration has SHIPPED (SPEC-FTR-03)'. Fix direction is a decision, not a patch: either integrate a real MLS library (cisco/go-mls or equivalent) behind the existing API, or rename/reframe the feature honestly (e.g. 'workspace-sealed messages', document the actual key model) and stop claiming SPEC-FTR-03 shipped. A cross-member encrypt->decrypt round-trip test is the missing gate that would have caught this.
reasoning: Filed by the 2026-09-20 dogfood run (stand-in lane): real two-user API walkthrough; the run never modifies code — findings become rows for the foreman.
worker_summary: Interim honest group-key model: persistent mls_groups.group_secret (migration 000048, nullable, lazily backfilled under a conditional-update race guard), domain-separated AES key SHA256('mls-app-key-v1'||secret) shared by Encrypt/Decrypt, secret rotated on JoinGroup/LeaveGroup/RemoveMember/CommitProposals via advanceEpoch, GetEpochSecret now persisted. New tests TestMLS_CrossMemberRoundTrip / TestMLS_RemovedMemberCannotDecryptFuture / TestMLS_GetEpochSecretPersisted all PASS (0 SKIP). Dated interim-model amendments in README + SPEC-FTR-03 + internal/mls/types.go: not RFC 9420, no forward secrecy within an epoch, no post-compromise security. AGENTS.md untouched (protected).

title: [P2] MLS provisioning is disjoint and half-API: MLS keys on the profiles TABLE which has NO API creation path (SetProfile writes the unrelated profile_route name-routing table), while POST .../mls/key-packages happily accepts and stores PRIVATE keys server-side; commit-proposals bumps epoch without any ratchet
detail: Found while driving MLS live (dogfood 2026-09-20, HEAD 85eaf18): (a) The only profiles-table creation path in the repo is a SQL seed in mls_integration_test.go (owner zero-UUID) - an API client cannot create the rows the MLS FKs require; I hand-seeded with that SQL. (b) The API's POST /workspaces/{ws}/profiles (SetProfile) writes profile_route (name-keyed routing, one-active-per-workspace - activating Bob's profile deactivated Alice's), a different concept that never intersects MLS. (c) GenerateKeyPackage request schema includes private_key, and the handler validates then stores material server-side - a client-held-secret model would never transmit it; the shape implies server-side crypto of the stub kind. (d) POST .../mls/commit-proposals returned 204 and bumped epoch 1->2 with zero proposals after DeleteAll - no ratchet semantics, epoch churn alone invalidates in-flight ciphertexts (hit ErrEpochMismatch mid-flow because join bumps the epoch). Fix: single profile concept with an API creation path, drop private_key from the wire, make commit a no-op-with-409 when no proposals, document epoch-bump-on-join for clients.

title: [P1] reference-proxy --token + --require-auth-user/password (the README-documented secure mode) never injects: validated Basic header suppresses Bearer injection
detail: Production-deploy dogfood 2026-09-22: ran the README §Production auth recipe verbatim — reference-proxy.py --dist frontend/dist --api ... --token <jwt> --require-auth-user/--require-auth-password — built PWA at HEAD 027f3b1b. Every proxied API call returned canopyd 401 TOKEN_MISSING. Root cause (deploy/reference-proxy.py): _handle() validates the Basic gate but never strips the Basic header; _proxy() then sees a client Authorization present (the Basic credential) and skips injection per "client sent none". Browsers auto-attach Basic after the 401 challenge, so the documented secure mode dead-ends for real users. Evidence: same proxy without Basic injects fine (200 with data); with Basic+token every call 401s; a plain Basic header with no gate also suppresses injection (passthrough arm). The deploy/tests suite only covers gate-less injection (ProxyTokenInjectionTests) and never the Basic+token combo. Fix: strip Authorization after successful Basic validation (or strip only the Basic scheme before the inject check), and add an integration test: gate+token → upstream sees Bearer, not Basic.
reasoning: P1 from the 2026-09-22 production-deploy dogfood: README-secure-mode proxy (--token + HTTP Basic gate) forwarded the gate Basic credential upstream, which suppressed Bearer injection (401 TOKEN_MISSING on every call). Picked over DF-49 (P2, pre-existing test bug) and the bunker/fleet-infra QA rows. Fix: strip Basic-scheme Authorization at header-copy time; inject Bearer only when no upstream Authorization remains (client Bearer still passes through and still suppresses injection; Basic stripped even without --token); docstring amended. title: [P3] MCP/REST asymmetry: bogus tree_id over MCP surfaces a raw PG FK error labelled "database unavailable"; REST returns clean NOT_TREE_MEMBER
detail: API dogfood 2026-09-22: create_node with tree_id 00000000-...-09 via MCP tools/call returned JSON-RPC error -32000 "create node: tree service: database unavailable: insert node: ERROR: insert or update on table \"nodes\" violates foreign key constraint \"fk_nodes_tree\" (SQLSTATE 23503)" — the same input over REST returns 403 NOT_TREE_MEMBER "you are not a member of this tree". Two defects in one: (a) the MCP path skips the membership precheck the REST path performs and lets the DB reject; (b) service layer maps that FK error to "database unavailable" (wrong class — the DB is fine, the request referenced a nonexistent tree). Fix: run the same membership/existence gate on the MCP dispatch path; reclassify FK 23503 on nodes insert as not-found/forbidden rather than unavailable. Minor sibling: unknown fields on tree-create return generic INVALID_BODY "must be valid JSON" — the GAP-053/072 field-naming fix covers node endpoints only.
reasoning: MCP create_node had no tree-membership gate (REST has TreeMembershipMiddleware), so a bogus tree_id hit PG and surfaced the raw fk_nodes_tree 23503 error wrapped as "database unavailable". Fix: TreeMemberChecker gate (IsMember/IsTreeDeleted) in toolCreateNode, membersRepo wired into NewMCPHandler (server.go:483); nodes-insert FK 23503 on fk_nodes_tree classified to ErrTreeNotFound (db + service layers, constraint-name-guarded) so the -32000 message is a request error; connection failures still map to database-unavailable. title: [P1] Export->import is dead for any tree with a soft-deleted node: export omits deleted nodes but keeps their edges, import rejects 'edge references node not in import payload'
detail: Dogfood 2026-09-24b (synthesis angle). Repro: fresh tree, 1 reply, DELETE the reply, GET /api/v1/trees/{id}/export -> nodes:1 with 1 edge whose targetId is not among node ids (verified jq). POST /trees/import with that payload -> 400 VALIDATION_ERROR 'export service: edge references node not in import payload'. Same failure on a real synthesis tree where one merge source was deleted mid-run (5 nodes / 9 edges exported, import refused). Clean trees round-trip fine (import 200 treeId nodeCount=2 edgeCount=1), so the happy-path tests pass while every pruned real tree is un-importable. Fix direction: either include deleted nodes in export (tombstoned) or drop edges referencing excluded nodes; add a round-trip test with a deleted node.

title: [P1] POST /trees/{id}/sync/snapshot returns 500 INTERNAL_ERROR whenever the current tree-state hash already exists (duplicate-key on idx_snapshots_tree_hash instead of idempotent return)
detail: Dogfood 2026-09-24b. Repro: POST /trees/{id}/sync/snapshot twice in a row, or once right after any mutation (mutation-triggered auto-snapshots in internal/sync/engine.go:130,161 usually insert first) -> 500. journalctl: sync request failed error='snapshot: insert: ERROR: duplicate key value violates unique constraint "idx_snapshots_tree_hash" (SQLSTATE 23505)'. internal/db/snapshot_repo.go CreateSnapshot does a plain INSERT and lets 23505 bubble; handler maps it to INTERNAL_ERROR. Verified the snapshot itself is correct (recomputed the SPEC-DM-02 hash from nodes/edges: matches stored). Fix direction: ON CONFLICT (tree_id, hash) DO NOTHING + return the existing row (200), or 409; never 500 for 'snapshot already exists'.

title: [P1] Plugin registration 500s with the documented dev JWT (sub=user UUID): plugin_registry.author_profile_id REFERENCES profiles(id) and the FK violation is masked as INTERNAL_ERROR
detail: Dogfood 2026-09-24b. README 'Authentication (dev mode)' provisions dev identity with JWT sub=00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001 (user UUID) and says plugins just work. POST /api/v1/plugins/ with a manifest-valid plugin + that token -> 500 INTERNAL_ERROR every time (deterministic, 3/3). Root cause: internal/plugin/repo.go Register inserts author_profile_id = the JWT subject; plugin_registry.author_profile_id REFERENCES profiles(id) (migration 000022) and the user UUID is not a profile id; internal/handler/plugin_handler.go fail() default case masks the FK error. Minting the same JWT with sub=<dev profile UUID> (01a0d018-8c71-76ce-9ea4-b4f835328400) -> 201. Every OTHER surface (trees/nodes/merge/context/sync) works with the user-sub token, so only the plugin path diverges from the documented quickstart. Fix direction: resolve user->profile in the plugin service (like profile_route does), or surface the FK error as 400 INVALID_REQUEST naming the subject.

title: [P2] Response-envelope drift vs docs/API.md on three routes: plugin versions returns bare array (docs: {plugins:[...]}), import returns flat summary (no documented shape), workspace profile mapping rows lack any profile id field
detail: Dogfood 2026-09-24b, found while consuming real payloads: (1) GET /api/v1/plugins/{name}/versions -> bare JSON array; docs/API.md 'List Plugin Versions' promises {"plugins":[...]}; the plugin LIST route does return {plugins:[...]}, so clients cannot assume either shape. (2) POST /trees/import returns {treeId,rootNodeId,nodeCount,edgeCount,topicCount,resolvedRefCount} with no 'tree' wrapper; docs' Export/Import section documents no response shape at all. (3) GET /workspaces/{id}/profiles rows carry workspaceId/profileName/displayName/isActive/mappedAt/lastUsedAt but NO id — the mapped profile cannot be referenced by id from the response (needed for e.g. plugin actor_profile_id). Fix direction: align versions route to the documented {plugins:[...]}, document the import response, add profile id to the mapping route (or document its absence).

title: [P2] Tree detail node_count disagrees with node list and graph stats (counted 1 vs 5 on the same tree): appears to be a root-child count, undocumented and confusing
detail: Dogfood 2026-09-24b. GET /trees/{id} -> node_count:1 while GET /trees/{id}/nodes -> 5 nodes and GET /graph/trees/{id}/stats -> active_nodes:5, stable across every mutation of the session (synthesis tree: root + 2 replies + 2 synthesis nodes). Export of the same tree says 5 nodes. Any UI or client trusting tree detail's node_count under-reports the whole branch depth. Also noted (unfiled, minor): GET /plugins/{id} returns 404 PLUGIN_NOT_FOUND for existing non-active rows (WHERE id=$1 + handler maps db.ErrPluginNotFound), while versions/activate resolve the same rows — only the metadata 404 is off, source-404-on-non-active is documented. Fix direction: make node_count the active-node total (or document the root-child semantics), and let GET /plugins/{id} return any-status rows per its own docs.
